Maria C: Hey @billing, saw a weird delta between the live dashboard token usage and the monthly invoice for acct `org_acme_inc`. Dashboard shows ~1.07M tokens for March but invoice billed 1.29M. Can someone take a look?
Leo H: thanks for flagging — do we have any short windowed spikes or known streaming billing quirks?
Maria C: Not obvious in the time-series. The spike is mostly split across many small streaming requests (SSE) from one customer. They also reported a lot of client disconnects.
Amanda S: @Maria C can you capture a couple of request IDs and sample timestamps? streaming requests tend to emit many partial chunks. If we double-count chunks + final chunk it could inflate tokens.
Maria C: Pasted two request IDs they provided: `req_3421f` at 1729548002 and `req_3429a` at 1729552107. Customer says client cancels mid-stream (ctrl-c) then reconnects.
Jose P: quick note — billing pipeline currently sums tokens per "generation event" emitted by the runtime. Streaming chunks are also emitted as generation events with token deltas. There was a prior fix to avoid double-counting when final event repeats tokens, but cancellations may leave orphaned partials.
billing-bot: AUTO: Invoice mismatch alert raised for org_acme_inc (delta 208k tokens). Ticket #BILL-438 created.
Maria C: Repro steps I used to emulate the customer's behavior (Linux):
```
# open an SSE stream and cancel after partial
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large","stream":true,"prompt":"long prompt..."}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# wait for a few chunks then ctrl-c
```
I saw several chunk events and then a 499 in the proxy logs when I cancelled.
Leo H: logs show for req_3421f we emitted 27 chunk events (token_deltas: 18,12,9,10...) then a final event with token_count=120. If billing summed all chunk token_deltas + final token_count we would double-count. Need to confirm whether final is incremental or absolute.
DevOps: checked the runtime traces — final event is supposed to be incremental (not cumulative), but a race during client disconnect can cause the commit path to emit both partials and a final summary metric. There is also a gap where the connector retries the request and that creates a new request_id with overlapping tokens.
Amanda S: For support triage — request these from the customer: a) request IDs and timestamps, b) whether they used a proxy/load balancer that retries clients automatically, c) client library version. This helps find retry-caused duplicates.
Jose P: Proposed short-term mitigation: in billing ETL, dedupe generation events by (request_id, token_index_range) and prefer the event with final=true. That should prevent chunk+final double counting. Longer-term: runtime should emit a terminal metric only once and mark partials as ephemeral.
Maria C: I've asked the customer for the logs and client info. Opening BILL-438 with these steps and assigning to infra and billing.
Leo H: Action items: @DevOps to run a 7-day job to find request_ids with overlapping token ranges; @billing-bot to compute how much to credit if dedupe applied; @Jose P to draft a patch for ETL dedupe.
billing-bot: NOTE: BILL-438 assigned to infra and billing.
Amanda S: One more thing — recommend we add explicit stream-end telemetry (stream.end_reason: completed|client_cancel|timeout) to improve postmortem accuracy.
Maria C: Thanks — will update the customer with the ask and ETA. :thumbsup:
